You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity

**Company:** Corvale Mobility (fictional name; intercity rail and coach operator)
**Location:** Kraków, Poland (contract, remote-friendly; occasional office days)
**Engagement:** Service agreement (B2B / freelance), not an employment contract
**Rate:** 95 – 125 PLN per hour

## The engagement

Corvale is preparing a new generation of trains and needs a cloud infrastructure engineer for the team that links the vehicles to the company's cloud platform. You will help shape the architecture from the start and take it to production.

## Scope

- Design, build and operate the cloud infrastructure that links on-board train systems with backend services: telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and remote content updates
- Maintain the infrastructure-as-code repository (Terraform with Terragrunt), keeping it tidy and approachable
- Lead technical proposals across backend and infrastructure from idea to production
- Contribute to system design and challenge decisions with arguments
- Set up secure train-to-cloud communication (mutual TLS, certificate management, network design)
- Agree interfaces and responsibilities with train manufacturers' engineers
- Support backend developers in deploying services that are easy to monitor and run
- Keep the platform observable, reliable and secure

## Requirements

- Hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation
- AWS preferred; other major clouds acceptable
- Strong Terraform and Terragrunt
- Good understanding of systems architecture and system design
- Networking knowledge, including mTLS and SSL/TLS
- Practical security awareness
- Experience leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along
- Strong analytical thinking and clear communication

**Nice to have:** IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack background (JVM preferred), Linux and virtual machines.

## Working model

Independent contractor, invoicing monthly for agreed services.

# COMPANY INFORMATION (web search results the writing tool had)

URL: https://corvale.example/press/workplace-awards
Corvale Mobility received several workplace culture awards based on an anonymous employee survey. Categories included innovation, work-life flexibility, purpose and values, professional development and employee appreciation. The people team said employees describe the culture as collaborative, fast-moving and open to new ideas, and that it will keep acting on survey feedback.

## Corvale Careers - Home
URL: https://careers.corvale.example
Why Corvale
1 International teams with shared goals.
2 Technology first: we use software to change how people travel.
3 Sustainability as part of growth.
4 Teams that solve problems together.
5 Ownership: you shape your own career path.
Locations: technology offices in Kraków and two other Central European cities, plus operations offices across the network.
Our values: Lead, Shape, Own, Enjoy the journey.
Many technology roles are open to independent contractors as well as employees. Employees can work hybrid and get travel benefits on the company's own network.

## About Corvale Mobility
URL: https://corvale.example/about
Corvale Mobility runs long-distance buses and a growing passenger-rail service in Central Europe. It uses an asset-light model: regional partners operate many routes while Corvale runs the booking platform, network planning and brand. Corvale has ordered a new train fleet to enter service later this decade, and scaling data and machine-learning use across the platform is a strategic priority.

## About Corvale: bus and rail operator
URL: https://corvale.example/company/leadership
Corvale was founded by a small group of transport and software people and is still led by its founders. Technology and people functions report to one chief officer, and the company describes itself as engineering-led, with teams that own their systems end to end.

## Corvale Mobility
URL: https://companies.example/profile/corvale-mobility
Corvale Mobility
Website: corvale.example
Headquarters: Kraków, Poland
Industry: Software development and transportation
Company type: Privately held
Description: intercity bus and rail travel with online booking, trip tracking and travel extras.

# CANDIDATE MATERIAL GIVEN TO THE WRITING TOOL
The tool was given only these documents about the candidate:

## CANDIDATE'S PORTFOLIO (projects and past work)
PROJECT: Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments (Odrava Health, 2023-2024)
- Every merge request gets its own short-lived environment (app + PostgreSQL + seeded data) deployed via Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Environments are destroyed automatically after merge or 48h of inactivity.
- QA and product can review features before merge; e2e tests run against the environment.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

PROJECT: CI Pipeline Speed-up (Odrava Health, 2022)
- Profiled the pipelines of three teams and parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split e2e into a separate stage.
- Average pipeline time 38 -> 14 minutes; monthly CI runner cost down about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

PROJECT: Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps (personal, 2024-2025)
- Three Raspberry Pi 5 nodes running k3s; all apps deployed from a Git repository with Argo CD.
- Prometheus + Grafana + Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, cert-manager for TLS.
- Infrastructure for a small VPS on Hetzner provisioned with Terraform (personal account).
- Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).

PROJECT: Flaky Test Dashboard (Odrava Health, 2023)
- Collected test results from CI into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests per team.
- Flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams started fixing the top offenders.
- Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.

EXPERIENCE: QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) at Odrava Health Software (2021-Present)
- Owns GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral environments for three teams.

EXPERIENCE: QA Engineer at Brightmill Software House (2019-2021)
- Selenium/Java regression automation, Jenkins nightly jobs.

## CANDIDATE'S EARLIER COVER LETTER (written for a different, earlier job application)
Hello Odrava Health Software team,

I'm applying for the QA Automation Engineer role.

I have been a QA engineer at Brightmill Software House for two years, testing web and mobile applications for different clients. On our largest project I introduced the first automated regression suite, written in Java with Selenium, and set up Jenkins to run it every night. Before that, a full regression took two people three days.

What I like most about automation is that it changes how a team works, not just how fast it tests. I want to work on a product team rather than for changing clients, and health software appeals to me because quality really matters there.

I have started learning Python and pytest because I saw your team uses them, and I already rewrote a small part of our API tests in Python as practice.

Thank you for your time and I hope to hear from you.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

## CANDIDATE'S OWN FREE-FORM NOTES
career switch notes (qa -> devops)

- studying for CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator). exam booked for Jan 2027. NOT passed yet
- did the "Terraform Associate" practice tests but didnt take exam
- no AWS/GCP/Azure at work. only personal Hetzner VPS + free tier AWS for learning (EC2, S3 basics)
- never been on production on-call. did join 2 incident calls as observer
- at Odrava the platform team (3 people) runs the k8s cluster. I have namespace-level access, I write helm charts for test envs, not the cluster itself
- I wrote the internal "how our CI works" doc, people use it in onboarding
- want junior/mid devops or platform role, ok with title drop to junior
- mentored 2 QA interns in 2023
- ISTQB Foundation Level cert, 2019

# CANDIDATE'S OWN WORK-ARRANGEMENT PREFERENCE
(not given: the candidate stated no preference, so they count as open to the job's arrangement)

- Configured environments to be automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity; QA and product teams use them to review features before merge, and end-to-end tests run against them.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | 2019–2021

SELECTED PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal Project | 2024–2025
- Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and operated applications through GitOps on a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster; configured Argo CD, Traefik ingress, cert-manager for TLS certificate management, and Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki monitoring.
- Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Created short-lived merge-request environments for feature reviews and end-to-end testing, with automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team; the flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed leading offenders.
- Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30% across three teams.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

CERTIFICATIONS
- ISTQB Foundation Level, 2019

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
- Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam scheduled for January 2027; not yet certified
- HashiCorp Terraform Associate — practice tests completed; exam not taken.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER (text)
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. In my current work as a QA Automation Engineer at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and automate Kubernetes-based test environments used by three teams. I’m looking to build further on this infrastructure experience, and the opportunity to help shape the platform connecting a new train fleet with cloud services is particularly compelling.

At Odrava, I built merge-request environments with an application, PostgreSQL, and seeded data, deployed through Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. I automated their cleanup and enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against the environments. I also profiled CI pipelines across three teams, reducing average run time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by about 30%. To make test quality more visible, I built a Python and PostgreSQL process and Grafana dashboards that helped teams reduce the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.

My infrastructure experience includes namespace-level work on a Kubernetes cluster operated by a platform team, TLS certificate management with cert-manager in a personal k3s and GitOps project, and provisioning a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform. I have also built familiarity with AWS EC2 and S3 fundamentals through learning. I document technical processes for others—in my current role, I wrote the CI guide used for onboarding—and have mentored two QA interns. These experiences have strengthened my ability to make infrastructure easier to use, review and operate collaboratively.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in CI/CD, Kubernetes test infrastructure, automation and observability could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

(The tool's messages are shortened; the user's replies are complete.)

USER: <path to job ad>

TOOL: Would you like to generate the CV or the cover letter first?
USER: Please write my CV first, then the cover letter.

TOOL: The CV still has placeholders for details I do not have: [EMAIL], [PHONE], [LINKEDIN]. Reply with the details to fill in, or tell me which ones to leave out. An empty reply makes the PDF as it is.
USER: I'd rather leave those details out.

TOOL: Your CV is ready. Would you like me to create a tailored cover letter for the Corvale Mobility role, or do you have feedback on the CV?
USER: Thank you. Now please write the cover letter.

TOOL: Both your CV and cover letter are ready. Would you like any changes to either document, or are you satisfied with them?
USER: Thanks, that is all. Please exit.
